title: Browser DevTools mastery (used in every phase)

plan.summary: Browser developer tools let a frontend developer inspect, debug, measure and fix a live page in the browser.

prerequisites.bridge: The DOM is the tree of objects the browser builds from HTML.
The browser sends a request; the server returns status, headers and body.
The call stack lists the functions running now, newest on top.

outcomes: Explain how the cascade produces an element's computed styles.
Debug async code with breakpoints, the async call stack and source maps.
Explain each timing phase of a request in the network waterfall.
Find a long task and a memory leak from traces and heap snapshots.
Build a CLI that triages HAR, trace and Lighthouse files against budgets.
Decide when to use Firefox, Safari or a real device instead of desktop Chrome.

lesson_outline.title: Elements and Styles: from the DOM to computed styles
lesson_outline.visual_reason: The cascade turns several matching rules into one computed value; a diagram traces one property from rules to the box model.
lesson_outline.interaction_goal: Predict which rule wins for one property, then check the Computed pane.

lesson_outline.title: Console power use
lesson_outline.visual_reason: The Console reads and changes the live page; a diagram shows which utility reads which part of page state.
lesson_outline.interaction_goal: Pick the console utility that answers a given question about the page.

lesson_outline.title: Sources panel: breakpoints and async call stacks
lesson_outline.visual_reason: A race condition shows only when execution pauses at the right place; the learner sets breakpoint types and watches the async call stack and scope change.
lesson_outline.interaction_goal: Choose a breakpoint type, run the race, and read the async call stack to find the bug.

lesson_outline.title: Source maps and local overrides
lesson_outline.visual_reason: A source map links each position in the shipped bundle to a position in an original file; a diagram traces one minified position back to its source line.
lesson_outline.interaction_goal: Map one bundle position back to the original file and line, then predict what DevTools shows without the map.

lesson_outline.title: Network panel: reading the waterfall
lesson_outline.visual_reason: Each request moves through queueing, DNS, connection, TLS, waiting and download; throttling changes the bar lengths the learner watches.
lesson_outline.interaction_goal: Change throttling and cache state, then predict which timing phase grows.

lesson_outline.title: Performance panel: traces, long tasks and Web Vitals
lesson_outline.visual_reason: A long task on the main thread delays the next input and paint; the learner records traces with different CPU throttling and finds the task in the flame chart.
lesson_outline.interaction_goal: Record a trace, find the long task in the flame chart and see INP change after a fix.

lesson_outline.title: Memory panel: finding a leak with heap snapshots
lesson_outline.visual_reason: A leak is an object still reachable from a root; a diagram shows the retainer path that keeps a detached DOM node alive.
lesson_outline.interaction_goal: Follow the retainer path from a GC root to a detached node and name the reference to remove.

video.reason: Finding a leak is a sequence: take a snapshot, repeat the action, take a second snapshot, compare, follow the retainer path.

lesson_outline.title: Application panel: storage, service workers and bfcache
lesson_outline.visual_reason: Several storage areas hold page state with different lifetimes; a diagram places each one and the service worker between page and network.
lesson_outline.interaction_goal: Sort each piece of state into the storage area that holds it.

lesson_outline.title: Lighthouse, Coverage, Rendering and the other panels
lesson_outline.visual_reason: Each panel answers one kind of question; a diagram maps a symptom to the panel that measures it.
lesson_outline.interaction_goal: Match a reported problem to the panel or audit that measures it.

lesson_outline.title: Firefox and Safari developer tools
lesson_outline.visual_reason: The browsers differ in what their tools do best; a diagram compares the strongest tool per browser.
lesson_outline.interaction_goal: Choose the browser whose tools fit a given debugging task.

lesson_outline.title: Debugging on real phones and device clouds
lesson_outline.visual_reason: Remote debugging connects desktop DevTools to a browser on a phone; a diagram shows the connection path for Android and iOS.
lesson_outline.interaction_goal: Order the steps to inspect a page on a USB-connected phone.

mini_projects.use_case: A support engineer gets a minified production stack trace and maps each frame back to the original file and line with the source map.
A frontend team exports a HAR file from the Network panel and needs a report of the slowest timing phases, uncached requests and render-blocking resources.
A developer saves a Performance panel trace and needs the long tasks over 50 ms and the layout shifts listed with their times, to choose what to fix first.

capstone.name: perf-triage CLI
capstone.problem: A frontend team receives performance bug reports with a HAR file, a Performance trace and a Lighthouse JSON report; one Node.js CLI reads all three, checks them against performance budgets and writes a ranked triage report.

known: Workstation and editor, including editor breakpoint debugging (roadmap 00.2)
goals: master frontend engineering end to end from the N1 roadmap
learn visually and by experimenting with simulations
use DevTools in every later phase of the roadmap

curriculum.scope: Browser developer tools for a frontend developer: Chrome DevTools panels (Elements, Console, Sources, Network, Performance, Memory, Application, Lighthouse and the other panels), Firefox and Safari tools, and remote debugging on real devices.
